Numbers have always felt like more than numbers to me; they are the stories people and companies need to make smarter, better decisions. That curiosity about how data, trends, and storytelling come together is what drew me toward a career as a Data Analyst, where I can turn complex information into clear, actionable decisions for both businesses and my own team. I am originally from Spain, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. Across my academic and professional journey, I have completed 8 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in translating complex datasets into insights that support better decisions and measurable improvements for both the organisation and its customers.

My background has also shaped how I approach work. During my doctoral work, I had to use a method that was completely new to me; within a few weeks I was applying it confidently, and soon after that I was the person colleagues asked to walk them through it step by step. On another project, I developed a new approach to a problem my group had treated as unsolvable, and that method was later adopted by other teams. In addition, colleagues still consult me now and then when they run into questions in areas I have worked on before.

Outside of formal study, I have been drawn to the point where careful analysis meets practical impact. During one lengthy stretch of work, several setbacks threatened deadlines, and I stayed with it through each stage, adding extra hours when deadlines demanded it so that the work could still be completed properly. Through this, I have strengthened my communication, organisation, and attention to detail. I also value the shared side of data work: when I volunteered for a major undertaking outside my formal duties, I carried it alongside my regular workload for more than a year until it was completed. Looking ahead, I am eager to bring this combination of analytical curiosity, practical problem-solving, and genuine interest in clear, useful decisions to a Data Analyst role.

Clear, truthful storytelling matters because it helps people make sense of the decisions that shape everyday life. That belief is what drew me to journalism: a curiosity about people, processes, and the stories behind everyday decisions, together with a belief that careful reporting can help communities understand the world around them. For me, it is a profession that turns curiosity into public service by informing people clearly and responsibly. I am originally from Colombia, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500. Through that academic foundation and my professional experience, I have developed a strong interest in producing work that is accurate, grounded, and purposeful. One of my favourite memories captures why this work feels so personal to me: while covering a local community event, I brought along a family member, who unexpectedly recognised someone I was planning to interview through an old neighbourhood connection. What began as a routine assignment became a warm, unexpectedly personal conversation that showed me how closely journalism is tied to real relationships and shared experience.

My academic and professional path has also shown me how I work in practice. Across my work, I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing the importance of accuracy, structure, and clear communication. In one role, I had to use a technique that was new to me, so I learned it within a couple of months and then began applying it independently in my own work. On another assignment, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on, and I value those moments because they reflect the collaborative side of journalism. Just as importantly, I complete the work expected in my role and deliver it on schedule. Together, these experiences have prepared me to contribute thoughtfully as a journalist while continuing to grow through reporting that informs, connects, and serves the people most important.

I am now eager to bring this combination of curiosity, practical judgement, and audience-focused thinking to a Marketing Manager role, where I can continue building campaigns that connect audience needs with clear brand stories and contribute to growth in direct, measurable ways.
